title: trailboss --json live
description: The agents running now, one row per terminal or process. `live --pin X` and `live --unpin X` print the same rows, with the change made and `pinned` updated, so a frontend needn't look again (without --json: the same table). --pin takes a row's terminal or session and fails (exit code 1, a message on stderr, nothing printed or changed) when no running agent has it. --unpin takes either name of a row and lets go of its pin whichever name was pinned (both, if both were), or a pin by the name given when its agent is gone; a name not pinned changes nothing and isn't an error. `live --settle X`, `--unsettle X`, `--quiet X` and `--unquiet X` print the same rows too, with `settled` and `quiet` updated; --settle and --quiet take a row's terminal or session and fail like --pin when no running agent has it, and the undoing ones take either name of a row, like --unpin. `live --board` prints the rows grouped by state instead (see live-board).

background.description: Background jobs the agent left running, oldest first: Claude Code's background shells and monitors (while one of its processes holds the output open), Codex's processes started during a turn and alive after it ended. Read-only: nothing is stopped. null for agents whose jobs Trailboss can't tell apart.

kind.description: shell or monitor (Claude Code), process (Codex); more may be added.

label.description: What it runs, on one line, at most 80 characters: the call's description or command (Claude Code), the process's command line (Codex).

since.description: When its process started, in ms since the epoch; null when unknown.

context_pct.description: context_tokens over context_window, as a whole percentage; null when either is unknown, or the tokens exceed the window (a larger-context mode).

context_tokens.description: The prompt of the last response (input plus cache read and written): what the context held; null when unknown.

context_window.description: The context window in tokens the agent runs with: what Codex records; for Claude Code 200k unless its 1M-context mode is on (the last response's requested model ends in [1m], else --model or the settings' model does) or the context already holds more, capped at the price table's max_input_tokens; else the price table's max_input_tokens; null when unknown.

cpu_pct.description: CPU the agent's process tree uses, in percent of one core (over 100 on several cores), to one decimal; null when unknown (no /proc).

transcript.description: The transcript file the agent's session writes, when known (from the agent, else the index); null otherwise.

effort.description: The reasoning effort the agent runs at, where it records one: the transcript's latest (Codex, pi), else the launch flag (Claude Code --effort, Codex -c model_reasoning_effort, pi --thinking), else Claude Code's settings (effortLevel); null otherwise.

model.description: The model of the session's last response (as the agent names it); null when none is indexed yet, or for Copilot CLI (usage arrives when it ends) unless launched with --model.

needs.description: Why the agent waits on you, in a few words ("Plan to approve", a question's first words, "Run: npm test", "Rate limited", the question a finished turn ended on); null when it doesn't.

needs_kind.description: What kind of request `needs` is, with nothing from the transcript: plan, question, run, edit, read, fetch, search, tool, rate_limit, error, waiting or reply (a turn that ended on a question; more may be added).

pinned.description: The user pinned this terminal or session (`live --pin`); `live --unpin` with either name of the row lets go of it.

procs.description: How many processes the agent's tree has, itself included; null when unknown.

quiet_busy.description: Working with no progress for a while, but its processes are busy (a long build or test run): busy, not stuck. `stuck` is the same when they aren't busy.

quiet_min.description: Minutes without transcript progress, when `stuck` or `quiet_busy`; null otherwise.

retry_at_ms.description: When a rate-limited agent may try again (ms since the epoch), as its error stated it: a reset time, or a wait counted from the error. Only present when `needs_kind` is `rate_limit` and the error said when; nothing else from the transcript.

rss_bytes.description: Resident memory of the agent's process tree, in bytes (memory shared between its processes counted in each); null when unknown.

status_since.description: When the agent entered its current status, in ms since the epoch: as `events` last saw it change, else (working) when its turn started, at its prompt, else (at rest) when its last turn ended or its transcript last changed; null when unknown.

tokens_note.description: Why `tokens` isn't the session's total yet, when the agent writes usage only at the end (Copilot CLI: "not until it ends"); null otherwise. A 0 is then shown as null.

turn.description: The turn under way, or the last one finished, counted from the transcript; null without one.

turn_ended_ms.description: When that turn ended, in ms since the epoch; null while it's under way or unknown.

label.description: The label `trailboss start` gave the agent in this terminal; null for one it didn't start.

definition.description: The agent definition `trailboss start` started in this terminal; null for one it didn't start.

started.description: How many agents and tasks this row's session started directly (the first level of `trailboss sweep --parent` for it): tasks and agents started with it as their parent, and agents nested under its terminal or process. 0 for a row with no session.

unread.description: Whether the session has a finished turn you haven't seen: one that ended after the later of when you last marked it seen (`trailboss seen`) and your last prompt to it. false without a session.

unread_turns.description: How many of its finished turns are unread.

unread_since_ms.description: When its oldest unread turn ended, in ms since the epoch; null when none is unread.

branches_unread.description: How many sessions started from this one (by `branch` or `start`, ended ones included) have an unread turn.

alert.description: The first spending limit from the config's alerts this agent is over: its session's (session_usd), else its folder's today (folder_usd). The day limit (day_usd) is only announced as a spend_alert event, never put on a row. Absent when it's under them all, or none is set.

limit.description: session, folder or day; more may be added.

amount_usd.description: What was spent, at API-equivalent prices, rounded to the cent: the session's cost, or the folder's or everyone's today.

limit_usd.description: The limit crossed, from the config.

settled.description: Settled (`live --settle`): off the board until it needs you (a question, an approval, an error, a finished turn, a message typed into it, or it exits), when the settle is cleared. Only on rows with an agent; absent in older versions.

quiet.description: A background worker (`live --quiet`): its finished turns and questions don't count as needing you, on the board and in `events` (no `finished` event, and no `needs_you` event whose `needs_kind` is question or reply; `turn_finished` stays), but approvals and errors still do. Kept until `--unquiet`, its terminal is gone, or its session hasn't run for 30 days. Only on rows with an agent; absent in older versions.
